keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Kwantung row (its Japan shape holds 17 cells at the southern tip of Liaodong from 1905, per the Empire of Japan dossier). The page: 'on the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, including Dairen (Dalian) and Ryojun (Lushun/Port Arthur)', area '3,500 square kilometres'; the infobox gives no area. The shape is the box 121.2-122.2 E, 38.8-39.4 N cut to China (17 cells, 4,301 km2 on the grid, ratio 1.23), the box the Empire of Japan dossier uses. The South Manchuria Railway Zone (extraterritorial rights along about 885 km of railway, 1905) is not territory and not drawn.

region.text: the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, leased to Russia

ledger.note: March 1898: 'In March 1898 Russia formally leased the region for 25 years from China.' The page gives no day; the Foreign concessions page was silent too (a newspaper footnote dates the signing 28 March 1898 and was not used). Russia governed it as 'Russian Dalian'.

5 September 1905: 'Under the Portsmouth Treaty (1905)' Japan replaced Russia as leaseholder (infobox gives the Treaty of Portsmouth date as 5 September). The territory continues; the leaseholder changes. The Twenty-One Demands later extended the lease to 99 years (the page gives no year), the Kwantung Garrison became the Kwantung Army in 1919, and the 1935 census counted 1,034,074 residents, 168,185 of them Japanese nationals.

2 September 1945: the territory 'ceased to exist following the Surrender of Japan' (infobox: surrender 2 September); the last governor left office on 28 August 1945. The page gives no date for the Soviet occupation; it was 'handed over to the People's Republic of China on 16 April 1955'.

certainty.note: Fixed by treaty (1898 lease; 1905 Portsmouth), but no page gives the line; the box is a stand-in, within a factor of 1.23 of the page's 3,500 km2.

sources.title: Kwantung Leased Territory
sources.note: March 1898 Russian lease; 1905 Portsmouth; 99 years; Kwantung Army 1919; surrender 2 September 1945; handover 16 April 1955; area 3,500 km2; 1935 census; governors; capital Dairen.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from one page (the Foreign concessions in China page was opened and was silent on dates and areas; it is not cited). Cliopatria folds this land into the Empire of Japan row from 1905 (Empire of Japan dossier, 17 cells); the colony dossier overlaps it and, as a colony, is drawn in the vassal tint of its metropole. Not settled: (1) the page gives no day for the 1898 lease or the Soviet entry; (2) the page does not say who held the land 1898-1905 other than 'Russia' (the Russian Empire dossier is not mine); (3) the year of the 99-year extension (Twenty-One Demands) is not on the page; (4) the end: the page says the territory ceased to exist in September 1945, but the Soviet occupation ran to the 1955 handover, which the Empire of Japan dossier has as a loss to the USSR in 1945; this dossier ends in September 1945 and names the Soviet Union as the successor, with the PRC as a second successor. (5) The page's 25-year Russian term runs to 1923; Japan held it past that. Gazetteer: the Liaodong tip is a box cut to China; Dalian, Lushun and Port Arthur exist in other forms. Counterparts qing-dynasty (ea-08-a/b) and the Russian Empire are not mine.
